jurisdiction.venue: Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York (Commercial Division, Part 45)

headline: New York Court Orders Fled NovaTechFx Founders to Pay $1.37 Billion Over Crypto Pyramid Scheme Targeting Haitian Communities
deck: Commercial Division Justice Anar Rathod Patel entered $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and 9% prejudgment interest against Cynthia and Eddy Petion and three NovaTech entities after the couple defaulted and fled the country.

financials.prison_display: 0 Days (Civil Default Judgment; Founders Fled U.S.)

score_provenance.rationale: New York Supreme Court ordered $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and 9% prejudgment interest (120.5% of the $1,134,549,691 NovaTech principal) alongside permanent industry bans, yet with no admission of liability and both founders having fled the country with zero days in prison, the civil paper award leaves a complete custody gap.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: A Manhattan state judge entered a $1.367 billion default judgment ($1.135 billion disgorgement plus $232.5 million interest) against fled NovaTechFx founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion for defrauding over 11,000 New Yorkers and hundreds of thousands worldwide, with zero days in prison.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Soliciting life savings from church congregations and neighborhood chat groups for a phantom investment pool and boarding a one-way flight before the bill arrives
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Multi-decade state or federal larceny custody upon apprehension, versus an uncollected civil default judgment here
